messages:
jane-cs: Customer reported recurring 500s when using the tool-calling API for file_analysis. Happens only from Go client builds in prod. Error: "no matching tool found for args" even though payload includes "file" key.

matt: do you have example payload + SDK versions?

jane-cs: yes — customer sent this snippet (sanitized):
```json
{"tool": "file_analysis", "args": {"file": "UEsDB...base64...", "metadata": {"name": "report.pdf"}}}
```
They say Python & TS clients work fine; Go SDK calls route to fallback model instead of tool. SDK versions: go 0.6.2, py 0.9.1, ts 1.2.0.

liz: interesting. Can you paste raw request body as received by router (from logs) and any error trace?

jane-cs: router log: `WARN tool-selector: key collision for arg tags: [file, File] -> rejecting explicit match; selected default-model`. Full log attached to ticket.

raj: that sounds like Go marshalling adding struct tags? We recently landed a change to `json` tags for optional fields (PR #3482) where `File` becomes `file` but also the Go client may include both `file` and `File` in some cases when using encoded bytes vs typed wrapper. Could cause duplicate keys in the parsed map.

matt: if the tool selector treats duplicate keys as ambiguous and chooses fallback, that matches symptoms. Repro plan: get minimal Go snippet that serializes the args to bytes and send to local router to confirm duplicate keys. Can someone paste minimal repro code?

jane-cs: customer repro snippet (from their engineer):
```go
type FileArg struct {
    File []byte `json:"File,omitempty"`
    Metadata map[string]string `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
}
fa := FileArg{File: raw, Metadata: map[string]string{"name":"report.pdf"}}
data := map[string]interface{}{ "tool": "file_analysis", "args": fa }
body, _ := json.Marshal(data)
// POST to /v1/call
```
They say the Marshaler can produce "File" key (capital F) and some encoder paths produce "file" lowercase leading to two keys in the final payload when proxies/clients wrap/unmarshal.

liz: thanks — that repro is helpful. I can reproduce locally: Go marshal + a wrapper from our client lib that copies fields into `map[string]any` produced both keys. Router uses a strict key-set match for tool schemas which treats duplicates as collision.

matt: quick triage: is this a router bug (should tolerate case-insensitive key matching) or SDK bug (should normalize tags to snake/camel)? Which path is lower-risk fix?

raj: both plausible. Short term we should add a defensive dedupe step in the router: when keys are same ignoring case, prefer lower-case (or follow schema canonicalization) and log a warn with sample id. That avoids customer impact. Long term: patch Go SDK to normalize struct tags when building generic arg maps.

sre-bot: created internal issue INF-5843 with logs and repro. Assigned to @matt. ETA for router hotfix request: 24h.

matt: I'll draft the router patch to canonicalize keys (lowercase) and add a unit test: send payload with `file`+`File` -> expect match. Also will reach out to Go SDK owners to propose normalization in next minor release.

jane-cs: customer asked about mitigation: can we request they use py/ts for now? They prefer not to. Any faster workaround?

liz: temporary mitigation: ask customer to set args as raw `map[string]interface{}` with a single `file` key (avoid typed struct). I'll PM them the exact snippet.

raj: logging note — include a hash of the conflicting keyset in the warn so we can correlate future reports. Also add a metric for key-collision rate.

matt: awesome. I'll push a small router PR today and follow up here with PR link and rollout plan. Thanks all.
